newsitem.title: FINLAND: Dutch EU presidency skips London stop due to fog.
newsitem.headline: Dutch EU presidency skips London stop due to fog.

text.p: Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo, whose country is current holder of the European Union presidency, said on Thursday he hoped any isolation of Britain could be avoided as it approached a spring general election.
A fierce debate is raging in Britain over its approach to greater EU harmonisation and a planned European single currency and Prime Minister John Major must call an election by May 22.

Van Mierlo, who is on a tour of several EU capitals to introduce the six-month Dutch presidency of the 15-nation bloc, was prevented from landing in London by fog on Wednesday and instead flew to Helsinki earlier than scheduled on Thursday.

"I think we should avoid a culture of isolation -- isolation situations for the United Kingdom within their campaign," he told a news conference in the Finnish capital after a meeting with his Finnish counterpart, Tarja Halonen.
"Let's as much as possible forget about it and do our work," he added.

He called Britain's forthcoming election "a complication of the first order" for the Netherlands' EU presidency, but added that the best approach would be to try to avoid "winding up the files" as much as possible until after the poll to give Britain some leeway.
"The only thing we can do is express the hope that the British are able to have a campaign in which "Europe' doesn't figure too negatively," he said.
"The more negative Europe is in the campaign, the more problems the winner will have to negotiate in the short time left after the elections."

He said his only strategy ahead of the British poll would be: "Don't give the impression that you are busy making a Europe of the 14...That would be provocative and play a negative role in the campaign, and would not be to the advantage of Europe.
"Each country on the continent feels that the campaign will not diminish the chances for results for the better of Europe," he said. "So that is all we can do."
